references.text: God promises Jacob that He will be with him and protect him wherever he goes, and bring him back to this land. This is the original promise now fulfilled as God commands Jacob to return home.
God tells Isaac that He will be with him and bless him—a parallel promise of God's presence also given to Jacob when he is called back to his ancestors' land.
Jacob calls upon God's promise, reminding Him of the command to return to his land and family, and that God would do good to him.
God commands Jacob to go up to Bethel and settle there, continuing God's guidance to return to his ancestors' land.
Jacob makes a vow at Bethel, linking God's promise of presence and safe return to his faith, which is fulfilled when God calls him home.
Jacob expresses his desire to return to his own place and land, forming the immediate background for God's command to go back home.
Jacob directly quotes God's command from 31:3 in his prayer, confirming that he saw his actions as a response to God's promise of presence.
Jacob's prophecy about future restoration (48:21) confirms and completes the promise he himself received in 31:3, showing God's faithfulness across generations.
